plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues of this tree erupt in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. The blooms carpet the pavement beneath in purple as they fall, and the tree's fern-like leaves make a soft backdrop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking from October through November and sometimes lingering into December
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and across southern Africa and eastern Australia
plants.funFact: Native to South America, the jacaranda has become a signature of Pretoria, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of street trees.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This graceful evergreen shrub opens delicate, lightly fragrant flowers just as most gardens wind down for the year. Its blooms range from crisp white to rosy pink, with bright golden stamens at the center.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, typically October through December
plants.location: Gardens in Japan and the southeastern United States, where it is widely grown
plants.funFact: It belongs to the same genus as the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and sasanqua seeds are pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: The flame-red 'petals' that light up the holiday season are really colored leaves called bracts, which surround tiny yellow flowers. In warm climates it grows into a large, shrubby, open-air plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter, with color developing from November to January
plants.location: Southern Mexico, its native range, and warm gardens in places such as southern California and Hawaii
plants.funFact: It needs long nights of about 12 hours or more to color up, which is why it naturally reaches its full color around late November.
